subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the migration delete them when the suffix scheme changes?
rationale: Config backups may be the user's only recovery copy, and repository policy treats config migration and recovery behavior as compatibility-sensitive rather than an automation-only choice.

options.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to retain existing `.bak.N` files until they are converted into, or aged out by, the timestamped retention set.

options.title: Accept First-Run Pruning
options.body: Explicitly accept that first-run cleanup after upgrade may delete existing numbered backups in exchange for a clean timestamp-only scheme.

options.title: Keep Numbered Backups
options.body: Reject the timestamped naming change for now and keep the shipped numbered ring as the stable backup contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to retain existing `.bak.N` files until they are converted into, or aged out by, the timestamped retention set.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent config backup and recovery-path history plus prior review context for this exact migration decision.
